The 16-bit read spanning both bytes is what proves one 2-byte field rather than two 1-byte fields.

tag index for group 'bitm' (0x6269746d): MOV ECX,dword ptr [EDI+0x3c] then tag_get(0x6269746d, it) at 0x97dc1-0x97dca - the contrail's bitmap reference

UNSIGNED: zero-extended via the XOR ECX,ECX; MOV CX,word ptr [EDI+0x40] idiom at 0x97e15-0x97e17, then used as the low bound of a random sequence pick. Our lift at contrails.c:301 declares this int16_t (signed) - a lift-learnings section 24 class discrepancy to correct.

UNSIGNED: zero-extended via the XOR EAX,EAX; MOV AX,word ptr [EDI+0x42] idiom at 0x97e0f-0x97e11, then ADD AX,CX to form the exclusive/high bound from the +0x40 base. Our lift at contrails.c:302 declares this int16_t (signed) - same section 24 discrepancy.

notes: SIZE IS NOT PROVEN and is deliberately omitted. This is a tag definition, not a data_t pool element, so there is no element-size constructor argument to read; the highest offset merely observed is +0x42. Do not render a cs() size assert from this artifact. Recovering the size requires the 'cont' tag definition's total size from the tag-loading path or the tag group registration table.
UNKNOWN RANGES (never observed accessed): +0x00..+0x01, +0x18..+0x23, +0x2c..+0x3b, and everything beyond +0x43. No interpolation was performed across them.

FINDING to fix in src/halo/effects/contrails.c independently of any struct work: +0x40 and +0x42 are unsigned in the original (zero-extend idiom) but declared int16_t in our lift at contrails.c:301-302. Latent rather than active - it only diverges for sequence bounds >= 0x8000 - but it is a real width/sign fidelity defect of the class lift-learnings section 24 describes.

The +0x02 flags field is accessed both as one 16-bit value and as two individual bytes (+0x02 and +0x03). Bits proven so far: bit 0 scales +0x04; bit 3 (0x8) scales +0x10; bit 4 (0x10) scales +0x14; byte +0x03 bit 0 scales +0x24; byte +0x03 bit 1 scales +0x28. In 16-bit terms the +0x03 bits are bits 8 and 9.

Out of scope but recorded from the same disassembly (0x97db0): the referenced 'bitm' tag has its sequence tag-block count at +0x54 and the block's element size is 0x40 (tag_block_get_element(bitm_tag + 0x54, sequence_index, 0x40) at 0x97dfd), and a bitmap sequence element holds a signed 16-bit count at +0x22 (CMP DX,word ptr [EAX+0x22] at 0x97e09).
